fact: Legal description states the property is situate on the south side of Pine Street.
Legal description begins 230 feet westward from the west side of Eighteenth Street.
Legal description lists a front/breadth on Pine Street of 22 feet.
Legal description lists depth southward 90 feet to Waverly Street.
Legal description identifies the property as 1822 Pine Street, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
2013 deed references prior owners Stephen A. Mione and Tralan Muntean.
2002 deed form lists the house number and street name as 1822 Pine Street.
2002 deed lists Roland K. Bullard II and Sally S. Bullard as parties.
1985 deed includes the parties Michael Kosmin and Rod Goodwin, and Pine Associates.
1979 deed references Mary G. Sharpe Wilkes (widow) as prior owner in the chain of title.
Newspaper clipping titled "1822 Sold for $14,000" is dated May 11, 1893 (Philadelphia Inquirer).
Death notice reports Spencer Jr. died at 1822 Pine Street of scarlet fever (age listed as 7 years).
Rolin-Plumb wedding breakfast was served at the residence of the bride's parents on Pine Street (OCR reads "IS22 Pine street").
Equal Franchise Society luncheon tickets were available from treasurer Miss Martha Davis, 1822 Pine Street (price $1.50).
Mrs. Graham Spencer closed her country house at Kaolin, Chester County, and returned to 1822 Pine Street for the winter.
Duhring, Okie & Ziegler finished plans for alterations and additions to Mrs. Graham Spencer's residence at 1822 Pine Street.
Okie, Duhring & Ziegler awarded contract for alterations and additions to the residence of Mrs. Agnes Spencer at 1822 Pine Street; cost about $6,000.
Notice lists a fireplace job at 1822 Pine Street with a cost of $130.
Society listing notes an "At home" for Mrs. Henry C. Davis and the Misses Davis at 1822 Pine Street.
1854 deed abstract: PRESENT OWNER "Jno Roset"; FORMER OWNER "Jno McCrea"; DATE OF DEED April 1854. This is the document tying builder John McCrea to this house.
1854 deed abstract describes the lot as the south side of Pine Street, 230 feet west of 18th Street, 22 feet front, 90 feet deep to Waverly Street — the same dimensions recited in the 2013 deed.

1893 deed abstract records the chain of title in red ink: "John Roset by Will to Mary Ann Roset by Will to The Penna Co for Ins on Lives &c et al in Trust" — documenting continuous Roset family ownership from 1854 until the 1893 sale.
1893 deed abstract: PRESENT OWNER "Howard Spencer"; FORMER OWNER "The Penna Co for Ins on Lives &c et al"; DATE OF DEED 29 June 1893. The 1893 purchaser was HOWARD Spencer, not Graham.

1899 deed abstract: PRESENT OWNER "Agnes M. Spencer"; FORMER OWNER "William McLean, Henry Pleasants, Executors & Trustees under the will of Howard Spencer"; DATE OF DEED 3 April 1899. The 1899 conveyance came out of HOWARD Spencer's estate.

1899 deed abstract, reverse: Registry Office entered 6 April 1899; Lot No. 76, Plan Book 3S page 21, Pine Street, 7th Ward, Division 21 — matching the city registry number 003S210076. The house number is written as 1822.
1854 deed abstract, DATE OF DEED column, read from the image: "Ap. 21. 1854" — April 21, not April 1.

Methodological caveat for directory evidence: a city-directory listing establishes the LATEST date by which a household was at an address, not the date it arrived. Canvassers compiled volumes months before publication, so the 1855 volume reflects 1854 fieldwork, and absence from an earlier volume is not evidence the house was empty.

1854 deed abstract describes “all that certain lot or piece of ground” with the measurements. That phrase is PRE-PRINTED on the form — the 1893 abstract, for a house that indisputably stood, recites it identically — so the absence of a “buildings and improvements” clause is NOT evidence the lot was vacant. The abstract does not establish whether a house stood on 21 April 1854.
